High Fat Diet Linked to Higher Colon Cancer Risk, Early Research Indicates

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1281 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a latest study, researchers report that a high fat diet may potentially increase the risk of colon cancer.
  • The researchers from Arizona State University said a diet high in certain fats can cause lasting changes in intestinal stem cells that lead to the development of tumors and the possibility of colon cancer.
  • The study was conducted in mice, but the researchers noted changes in the DNA of intestinal stem cells that may explain their growth and survival.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a latest study, researchers report that a high fat diet may potentially increase the risk of colon cancer.

The researchers from Arizona State University said a diet high in certain fats can cause lasting changes in intestinal stem cells that lead to the development of tumors and the possibility of colon cancer.

The study was conducted in mice, but the researchers noted changes in the DNA of intestinal stem cells that may explain their growth and survival.

The researchers published their findings on November 12 in the journal Stem Cell Reports.

Sources indicate that the researchers said the study is key because 1 in 25 people develop colon cancer in their lifetime. In the United States, that translates into about 108,000 latest cases of colon cancer every year. About 55,000 males and 55,000 females are expected to die from the disease in 2026.

Experts not involved in the study say the research provides valuable information, but they have reservations about the results, as the findings do not yet apply to humans.

“The findings provide a potential mechanism linking diet to intestinal cancer development, but we need to be cautious about translating these results to humans,” noted Dalia Perelman, MS, CDE, a research dietitian at Stanford University in California.

Industry observers note that “We already have evidence from human studies that obesity and certain dietary patterns, particularly those high in processed meats and low in fiber-rich foods, are associated with increased colorectal cancer risk,” Perelman told Healthline. “This study adds a potentially important mechanism to investigate, but it does not establish that dietary fat itself increases colorectal cancer risk in humans.”.

Ketan Thanki, MD, a colorectal surgeon specializing in benign and malignant diseases of the colon, rectum, and anus at the MemorialCare Todd Cancer Institute at Long Beach Medical Center in California, shared similar views.

“This study provides a better understanding at the cellular level of how a high fat diet may contribute to colorectal cancer development,” Thanki told Healthline.

“Animal studies are an important starting point for understanding biological processes, but we must be cautious about directly applying their findings to humans,” he added. “Mice and humans share many cellular and biological mechanisms, which makes these studies valuable in identifying potential pathways involved in disease development. However, human diets, genetics, metabolism, and environmental exposures are more complex.”.

To reach their findings, the Arizona State researchers fed mice what the scientists described as a Western-style high fat diet for 6 months.

They then compared those results with those from mice given a low fat diet.

The researchers said the mice on the high fat diet gained more weight than the mice on the low-fat diet. They also developed more intestinal stem cells, and those cells grew at a more rapid rate.

They added that mice genetically predisposed to intestinal cancer who were fed a high-fat diet developed more and larger tumors.

The researchers noted changes in the DNA of intestinal stem cells that may help explain their increased growth and survival.

According to recent reports, they also pointed out that stem cell behavior returned to normal after high fat diet mice were switched to a low fat diet, although some DNA changes persisted. After four weeks, approximately 18% of these changes remained.

When mice were returned to a high fat diet, the researchers remarked their intestinal stem cells responded more promptly and strongly than those of mice exposed to the diet for the first time.

They concluded that the study suggests that maintaining a healthy, low fat diet may help regulate intestinal stem cell growth and reduce colon cancer risk.

Kristin Kirkpatrick, RD, president of KAK Consulting and a dietitian at the Cleveland Clinic Department of Wellness & Preventive Medicine in Ohio, wasn’t involved in the study but highlighted a particular aspect of the findings.

“What I found particularly interesting was that even after the mice returned to a low fat diet, some of the molecular changes persisted,” she told Healthline. “This raises questions about how our dietary patterns over time may influence long-term health.”.

Experts noted these upcoming findings are interesting but noted numerous caveats.

Sources indicate that “One important takeaway is that dietary habits over time matter,” mentioned Thanki. “Even if someone has consumed a high fat diet for years, making changes now may still provide meaningful health benefits.”.

“I also think these findings are particularly vital for children and adolescents, as establishing healthier dietary habits early in life may provide long-term benefits,” he added.

It has been revealed that however, Thanki noted that not all fats are the same. “The health risks depend partly on the type of fat consumed, how much is consumed, and what foods make up the overall diet,” he stated.

Industry observers note that “Diets consistently high in saturated fats, particularly those containing large amounts of processed meats, fried foods, and highly processed products, can contribute to obesity, elevated cholesterol, cardiovascular disease, and metabolic dysfunction. These factors can also contribute to chronic inflammation and may increase the risk of certain cancers, including colorectal cancer,” Thanki continued.

Perelman stated the diet used in the study was extremely high in fat, providing 60% of calories from fat, primarily from lard.

“We know that the health effects of dietary fats differ depending on their sources and fatty acid composition, and we cannot assume that a diet rich in unsaturated fats from foods such as olive oil, nuts, and seeds would produce the same effects,” she noted.

Perelman added that the researchers primarily studied stem cells from the small intestine rather than the colon.

“Although these tissues share some biological characteristics, they have vital differences, and we cannot assume that the same changes would occur in the colon,” she explained.

Finally, Perelman noted that “the mice consuming the high fat diet also gained weight, making it difficult to separate the effects of dietary fat itself from those associated with increased body fat and other metabolic changes.”.

Industry observers note that not all high fat foods are unhealthy. Some high fat foods that offer healthy benefits include:.

“The goal shouldn’t necessarily be to eliminate fat because our bodies need healthy fats for normal functioning,” stated Thanki. “Instead, people should focus on reducing saturated and trans fats while incorporating healthier unsaturated fats in appropriate amounts.”.

Thanki had several dietary suggestions. Among them:.

According to recent reports, “Consistency matters more than perfection. Even modest dietary changes, maintained over time, can have meaningful health benefits,” Thanki remarked.

It has been revealed that perelman agreed. “The overall quality of the diet matters. Diets that are very high in fat may displace other foods and nutrients that have important health benefits,” she stated.

“For colorectal cancer specifically, higher intakes of dietary fiber and whole grains have consistently been associated with lower risk,” Perelman noted.

“Therefore, rather than focusing exclusively on reducing fat, it is notable to consider the overall dietary pattern and whether it provides adequate amounts of fiber-rich plant foods and other beneficial nutrients.”.

Sources indicate that kirkpatrick agreed that the type of fat is what is important. “A Mediterranean-style diet that includes olive oil, nuts, seeds, and fatty fish can be relatively high in fat but is consistently associated with positive health outcomes,” she said.

“On the other hand, a diet high in saturated fat, processed meats, and ultra-processed foods may increase the risk of certain chronic diseases, particularly when it’s also low in fiber and other protective nutrients.”.

Kirkpatrick also noted that many lifestyle habits contribute to a person’s overall health.

“Our health is influenced by so many factors beyond diet, including how we manage stress, our sleep habits, physical activity, genetics, and overall lifestyle,” she said.

Aptera (SEV) completes its first customer solar EV — for its top crowdfunder

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1002 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that aptera (SEV) has finished building its first solar electric vehicle for a paying customer.
  • Recent findings suggest that it’s a real milestone for a company that has pushed back its delivery dates since 2022.
  • Recent findings suggest that aptera revealed today from its Carlsbad, California headquarters that it completed what it calls its first production solar electric vehicle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that aptera (SEV) has finished building its first solar electric vehicle for a paying customer. It’s going to Martin Hartono, the startup’s No. 1 “Accelerator” investor, and it’s being exported out of the US.

Recent findings suggest that it’s a real milestone for a company that has pushed back its delivery dates since 2022. And it comes a week after Aptera reported $9.2 million in cash against the roughly $25 million it notes it needs to start series production.

Recent findings suggest that aptera revealed today from its Carlsbad, California headquarters that it completed what it calls its first production solar electric vehicle. The car is finished in “Noir,” a matte black exterior, and was built for Accelerator #1.

According to recent reports, accelerators are investors from Aptera’s community funding program, where delivery priority goes to whoever invests the most. So the first customer car went to the biggest check.

Hartono is the CEO of GDP Venture, the Jakarta-based venture arm of Indonesia’s Djarum Group. Aptera didn’t say which country the car is going to, what he paid for it, or when it will actually be handed over.

In the release, Hartono noted Aptera is a fit for people who want to “minimize their energy consumption without compromising the ability to travel long distances.” Co-CEO Chris Anthony called it “the moment our team has worked toward for years” and said the manufacturer is working to finish more vehicles for early customers as soon as possible.

No number was given for how many more.

It has been revealed that the timing is interesting. Just seven weeks ago, Aptera cut its estimated cost to start production to about $25 million, down from $40 to $45 million, and said the first 40 production vehicles would start building by the end of 2026, with customer deliveries in early 2027 “subject to financing.”.

In a recent development, its Q3 report last week didn’t change that picture much. Aptera ended September with $9.2 million in cash, and $4.1 million of that is refundable reservation fees. It lost $14 million in the quarter, and its own filing indicates substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern “has not been alleviated.”.

On November 10, it priced a $6 million registered direct offering at $1.75 per share. SEV closed at $1.67 on Tuesday, with a 52-week high of $7.

Recent findings suggest that the solar side of the pitch holds up better. In August, TÜV Rheinland measured 4.23 to 4.75 kWh per day going into the battery from the car’s integrated panels in Carlsbad, which works out to roughly 40 miles of daily driving. But that conversion relies on Aptera’s 100 Wh/mile efficiency target, and today’s release itself notes that figure isn’t yet confirmed for production vehicles.

Industry observers note that the release’s risk factors are also worth reading. They list export, import, certification and registration requirements, state dealer licensing, single-source suppliers, and whether reservations will convert into binding orders. Shipping car No. 1 to an investor overseas sidesteps most of those for now.

Credit where it’s due. Aptera has a finished car built to a customer’s spec, which is more than Lightyear or Sono Motors ever got to before they ran out of money. We’ve followed this firm since it came back in 2019, and plenty of people (us included, at times) didn’t think we’d see this day.

A positive achievement, but the question remains: Is this essentially a hand-built prototype and a token delivery to one very rich customer, or is it the first of many more vehicles that will roll off an assembly line for regular people over the next couple months?

But I have to be honest, this looks more symbolic than like the start of a production ramp. This is a single vehicle, built before Aptera has raised the money it notes it needs for series production, and it went to the person who put the most money into the tech giant. That’s a thank-you and a good press release ahead of what will likely be another raise. It doesn’t tell us much about Aptera’s ability to build cars at a cost that works.

The real test is still the first 40 cars, and whether they reach regular reservation holders in the US. Aptera notes it needs about $25 million to get there. It has $9.2 million, $4.1 million of which customers can ask back for, and it’s raising money at under $2 a share, which means a lot of dilution for every dollar.

We want this to work. Ultra-efficient cars are the only way vehicle-integrated solar makes sense, and Aptera is the last serious attempt standing. So can it fund those 40 cars before the cash runs out?

It has been revealed that if you’re buying an EV, powering it with home solar can cut your fuel costs to nearly zero, even if your car doesn’t have panels built into the body like the Aptera. With electricity rates up almost 10% last year and expected to keep climbing, going solar is one of the best ways to protect yourself against rising costs. 💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that in bear life, as in human life, sometimes you just have to take a leap of faith. A brown bear (Ursus arctos) cub hanging around Anan Creek in Tongass National Forest in southeastern Alaska learned that this summer. Its mom, Gemini, was crossing the creek, and one cub jumped right in. But this cub? Not so sure. It stood waiting at the water’s edge, before jumping in.

In a recent development, for this forceful leap into the water, the park rangers have awarded Gemini’s little cub with the 2026 Yeet of Faith Award. For those keeping score at home, Gemini won this year’s helicopter mom award.

“Cubs learn at their own pace, and thanks to amazing recreation sites like Anan, we get to witness their tiny triumphs up close,” the rangers write.

Tongass National Forest’s rangers are awarding the Anan Bear Awards to the 39 bears spotted at the Anan Wildlife Observatory in Alaska over the summer.

Industry observers note that tongass is the largest national forest in the United States, and covers most of Southeast Alaska, including the state’s capital city of Juneau. The area includes Mendenhall Glacier (a popular destination for Alaskan cruises), numerous hiking trails, eagles soaring above, and plenty of bears on the hunt for food. One of the hotspots for wildlife is Anan Creek, home to one of the largest runs of pink salmon in Southeast Alaska. As such, the creek is a very popular dinner spot among black and brown bears.

According to Friends of Anan, 39 bears are known to feast on the salmon at Anan Creek. The population includes 31 black bears (Ursus americanus) and eight brown bears like Gemini and her cubs. Similar to their chubby counterparts farther to the north in Katmai National Park, the bears return each summer to gorge on salmon ahead of the long winter, and teach their cubs how to fish in order to survive. And also like the fat bears of Katmai, every bear around Anan Creek has their own habits and quirks.

In a recent development, the U.S. Forest Service tracks and documents every bear spotted at Anan, while explore.org’s cameras broadcast live streams of their behaviors.

  • Toyota revealed a latest compact pickup called the Corolla Cross Deck on Wednesday during its inauguration of a new production facility in Sococaba, Brazil, and it will enter production in the first half of 2027.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that toyota has had incredible success with pickup trucks in the United States of America. The Tacoma has become one of America’s perennial best-selling vehicles, while the Tundra has carved out a sustainable niche in America’s grueling full-size segment. But there’s arguably room for more.

In a recent development, rumors have long suggested Toyota is working on a compact, Ford Maverick-fighting pickup that would fill the truck lineup’s glaring need for a cheaper and more efficient option. Dealers have reportedly been asking Toyota for a compact pickup for several years. Mark Templin, Toyota’s COO in the United States, confirmed Toyota is “looking at” bringing a smaller pickup to the U.S. back in May 2025. And now, Toyota has just unveiled a newly introduced pickup that could fit that bill … for Latin American and Caribbean markets.

Toyota revealed a latest compact pickup called the Corolla Cross Deck on Wednesday during its inauguration of a new production facility in Sococaba, Brazil, and it will enter production in the first half of 2027. According to Motor1 Brazil, the Corolla Cross Deck shares a TNGA-C platform with the Corolla sedan and Corolla Cross SUV. Toyota did not provide full specs, but did reveal a hybrid version—likely featuring the 1.8-liter 122-horsepower powertrain Toyota uses for the Corolla Cross in that market.

Sources indicate that sadly, Toyota has not confirmed potential availability for the Corolla Cross Deck in the American market. The automaker did not respond to a Road & Track inquiry about its potential availability by the time of publication, but we’ll update this story if we receive a response.

Industry observers note that on paper, a Corolla-based compact pickup would likely be the easiest route for Toyota to bring a small, cheap pickup to the United States in the foreseeable future. Toyota already builds the Corolla and Corolla Cross at its Mazda Toyota Manufacturing Facility in Alabama; a new truck truck could be built on the same line—and even spawn potential rebadged variants for Toyota partners Mazda and Subaru.

It has been revealed that in the American market, the Toyota Corolla Cross uses 2.0-liter gas and hybrid engines. That powertrain could give Toyota options for a 169-horsepower base gas model truck—potentially starting below $30,000—and a 196-hp hybrid version that could eclipse 40 miles per gallon.

That stated, one could also see Toyota needing a different small truck approach to resonate with an American audience. One of Ford’s great innovations with the Maverick was that it looks more like the F-150 and Ranger than the Escape crossover it shared a platform with. And even if a upcoming Toyota pickup were to share its bones with the Corolla, Toyota may want to brand it as an extension of the pickup line, rather than the Corolla family.

Industry observers note that volkswagen introduced the ID. Buzz Beach, a fun spin on its electric van that’s built for camping and overnight stays. However, it won’t be cheap, starting at over $70,000.

Volkswagen’s original microbus became a cultural icon thanks to its open, customizable interior, making it perfect for large families, road trips, camping, and, of course, music festivals.

It has been revealed that the ID. Buzz brings the classic Type 2 microbus into the electric era with a retro-fresh style, modern tech, and a flexible, spacious cabin.

Building on its reputation as a symbol of freedom and adventure, Volkswagen is adding a latest member to the electric people mover lineup.

The new ID. Buzz Beach “brings adventure into the electric age,” Volkswagen noted after introducing the new variant on Thursday. Designed for camping, longer road trips, and overnight stays, the electric van will be available in 5-, 6-, and 7-seat configurations.

Volkswagen stated it sleeps two comfortably with a removable bed frame and a custom-fitting folding mattress.

The mattress is a decent size at about 6.5 feet long by 4 feet wide (2.0m x 1.2m), roughly the size of an average small double bed.

In the 5-seat configuration, the bed frame tucks away in the trunk, while in the 6- and 7-seat layouts, it’s stored vertically behind the third row of seats.

It has been revealed that for camping and other longer stays, Volkswagen added a new Overnight mode that uses the vehicle’s battery to provide up to 48 hours of continuous, off-grid climate control. The new mode can be accessed on the center touchscreen.

It also includes blackout curtains throughout the cabin and ventilation grilles on the front side windows.

Industry observers note that the ID. Buzz Beach offers vehicle-to-load (V2L) capabilities. A 230V power socket adaptor comes standard, letting you power an e-bike, charge a smartphone, run camping equipment, or power other external electronic devices. A camping connector is available as an added option.

To top it off, Volkswagen added a hidden foldable table and chairs set that can be tucked away without taking up internal space.

Volkswagen will open orders for the latest ID. Buzz Beach in the UK later this month, starting at £53,955 (excluding VAT), or about $71,000. Including VAT and OTR costs, it will start at £65,837, or roughly $86,500.

Nice product at the wrong price. If VW can't lower the price because of the cost, then it has a lot more work to do to compete in this market.

What about those in the US? VW introduced the 2027 ID. Buzz with a fresh Tourer model that was essentially the same as the Beach variant in the UK, with a fold-out mattress, Overnight mode, blackout curtains, and a table and chairs set.

Recent findings suggest that however, VW told its US dealers in September that it would be delaying the ID. Buzz’s return until the 2028 model year.

Recent findings suggest that the 2025 Volkswagen ID. Buzz started at about $60,000 in the US, which is one of the biggest reasons it failed to catch on with buyers. The original VW microbus was an affordable people mover.

Industry observers note that A custom camper variant would likely cost more than $70,000. Would you pay $70,000 or more for Volkswagen’s electric camper van?

#75244. Depression's Cruel Paradox: When What Helps Feels Impossible

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1114 w)

Depression's Cruel Paradox: When What Helps Feels Impossible

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1114 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Updated November 22, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.
  • There is a cruel paradox of depression: The very activities that might help you feel better are the very ones you feel least capable of doing.
  • According to recent reports, when my depression was at its worst, which meant my motivation was at its lowest, that was precisely when I needed to find ways to become active.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Updated November 22, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.

There is a cruel paradox of depression: The very activities that might help you feel better are the very ones you feel least capable of doing.

According to recent reports, when my depression was at its worst, which meant my motivation was at its lowest, that was precisely when I needed to find ways to become active. I knew what helped. But knowing and doing are two very separate things. Two things separated—in the case of depression—by a great distance.

In a recent development, I should go for a walk, but all I wanted was to hide under my covers. I should eat a salad, but all I wanted was to scarf down sweet potato fries. I should reach out to my friend Alana, but Netflix seemed like a better companion.

Recent findings suggest that making matters more challenging, if I did manage to set goals, they were usually unrealistic, which only served to reinforce the depressive cycle: setting a goal, not accomplishing it, feeling worse about myself, and withdrawing further. The wash, rinse, and repeat cycle ad nauseam.

I’ve discovered after many depressive episodes that it’s not about pushing through or pushing harder. It's about finding balance between compassionate acceptance of where I’m at, and identifying gentle, achievable action that will benefit me most.

Emma Morton, a psychologist at Monash University in Melbourne, and I were interviewed about strategies that interrupt the depressive cycle.1.

According to recent reports, morton explained that one evidence-based strategy is called behavioral activation. It aims “to break the cycle of lethargy and negative thoughts and behaviors that maintain depression.”.

She stated, "When we’re depressed, symptoms such as the loss of interest and enjoyment in your usual activities, combined with fatigue and lack of energy, can make our worlds become very small.".

I know this to be true. My bedroom, my TV, and the thoughts in my head—very negative thoughts at that—become base camp.

Sources indicate that morton acknowledged, “When we’re overcome by exhaustion, resting makes sense. When everything feels stressful, withdrawing can feel protective … Unfortunately, this kind of behavior maintains, rather than helps, a depressed mood. The more isolated from our environment we are, the fewer opportunities we have for connection and positive experiences that can help improve our mood. Instead, we can end up with more time for negative self-talk and rumination.”.

According to recent reports, I learned that, at its core, behavioral activation is about gradually increasing two types of activities: those that bring me—or used to bring me—some kind of enjoyment, and those that give me a sense of accomplishment. Or even better, activities that do both.

It has been revealed that activities that bring me a sense of mastery—a sense of self-efficacy—have great potential to lift my mood. They offer an opportunity to feel good about something or simply provide a distraction from my caustic inner thoughts and help pass the time.

I remember one particularly ugly depression, one loaded with all the bells and whistles: lack of motivation, self-hatred, self-sabotage, no self-esteem, no joy, unrelenting fatigue, and perpetual anxiety. You know the type: a nice combustible, masochistic mixture of all things unwanted.

It has been revealed that I began to practice behavioral activation and set goals. Early on, I saw the importance of letting go of the expectation that these small activities would make me feel better right away. This alone gave me motivation to carry on when I didn’t see the point.

In a recent development, it was the accumulation of small positive actions that began to improve my mood. Slowly, I would notice little blips of joy—ok, maybe not joy—but relief. Moments when the world felt a little brighter—if only briefly.

Sources indicate that the activities distracted me, helped pass the time, and helped me put one foot in front of the other. At first, a goal that made me feel good about myself might simply be putting my jeans and shoes on, instead of wearing sweatpants and slippers. My goal wasn’t even a walk—it was to change into something I might wear when and if I went for a walk. That’s how manageable I needed them to be.

Sources indicate that morton acknowledged this approach can sound boring and overly simplistic. “But it’s not,” she explained. “When paired with other evidence-based techniques, it’s a powerful tool that can disrupt the cycle.”.

Industry observers note that I easily judged myself when I thought about these goals. They were embarrassingly small and meaningless, weren’t they?

This inner hurdle had the potential to prevent me from even trying. In order to have a chance at any success, I needed to find a way to address it.

It has been revealed that self-compassion and gentleness were the antidotes. Another cruel paradox—these weren’t exactly in abundance when I was in the depths of darkness. It was true, in the past I was capable of more. But depression, like other illnesses, affects our ability to function. Maybe, at the time, those activity goals were the perfect size for me.

It has been revealed that when I couldn’t find compassion for myself—read most of the time—I borrowed it. I turned to my therapist, a friend, or read excerpts from helpful books like Pema Chodron’s When Things Fall Apart. Or, if I was lucky, a cuddle from a loving pup helped. They all reminded me that I'm worthwhile, just because I am. Period.

I would make a list. Monday: Have a shower. Tuesday: Talk with Petrina. Wednesday: Walk around the block with Lea. Thursday: Eat a homemade healthy dinner. Friday: Watch two hours of Grey’s Anatomy, not four.

According to recent reports, slowly, very slowly, over a period of weeks or months (yes, months—yowch—I know), I started to feel better, and the depression began to fade. Climbing out of my depression, though, wasn’t entirely due to the accumulation of small achievements. I was also taking my medication, seeing my psychiatrist and counselor, keeping my sleep on track, and meditating.

According to recent reports, we can’t force ourselves to feel better. That’s not possible—even if it were—it wouldn’t be helpful. But setting small, achievable goals that give our mood a chance to shift is. And lo and behold, those tiny actions add up and can gradually bring relief and eventually help us feel like ourselves again.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that while archivists previously digitized a similar collection related to the American Revolutionary War, the latest documents will help fill in knowledge gaps between early 19th century military events and the 1850 federal census.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that after 16 years of painstaking work, the National Archives and its collaborators have finally completed digitizing over 90,000 pension applications submitted to the United States government following the War of 1812. The project is more than just preservation for preservation’s sake. The roughly 2.8 million pages contain long-forgotten and missing details about 19th century Americans, their families, and their everyday lives.

Recent findings suggest that while archivists previously digitized a similar collection related to the American Revolutionary War, the latest documents will help fill in knowledge gaps between early 19th century military events and the 1850 federal census. Patricia Oxley, president of the Federation of Genealogical Societies (FGS), explained the project was also incredibly time-sensitive.

“In the specific case of the War of 1812 pension records, there is an added priority due to their frail state where not acting may mean sacrificing these for future generations,” Oxley stated in a recent announcement.

Sources indicate that the somewhat newly introduced United States of America declared war on the United Kingdom on June 18, 1812, citing objections to trade restrictions with France amid the Napoleonic Wars, as well as the Royal Navy’s impressment of American sailors. Although the conflict famously included a British attack on Washington D.C. that resulted in the burning of the White House and U.S. Capitol, little shifted geopolitically between the two nations following the ratification of the Treaty of Ghent on February 17, 1815. The U.S. tallied around 15,000 casualties, while the U.K. and Canada saw about 10,700 deaths. Another 9,000 Indigenous fighters died while enlisted between the two sides.

In a recent development, today’s military records are meticulously documented and stored digitally, but applying for benefits such as pensions was a much more labor-intensive process during the 19th century. With the burden of proof on each applicant, veterans were required to supply lengthy accounts of their service. Each War of 1812 pension file is liable to contain not just combat information, but the names and personal details of fellow soldiers, family members, spouses, and countless other relations.

“Our people have been asking for the War of 1812 pension records for some time, and I expect this collection to be very popular based on the rich war time detail it contains,” added Brian Hansen, general manager at Fold3, Ancestry’s military records service and National Archives collaborator.

The collection also includes a full-text search feature using handwriting recognition technology. This lets users explore the files based on every named individual, and not simply the primary veteran applicants. The pension records are presently available for free on Fold3’s website, and are being added to the National Archives catalog on a rolling basis.

In a recent development, correction 11/20/26 9:30 a.m. EST: A previous version of this article incorrectly stated the pension archive contained around 7 million files. This was based on an initial assessment from researchers in 2010. The article has been updated to reflect the more accurate tally.

As confirmed via premierleague.com, Sam Barrott will take charge of the match, with Adam Nunn and Lee Betts as his assistants, while Chris Kavanagh is fourth official. John Brooks is on VAR, assisted by Paul Howard.

The upcoming game is the Reds’ sixth home match in the top flight this season, and it’ll be the third to have had the Yorkshire native as the referee.

Upon learning that curious fact, Keith Hackett took to social media to endorse Barrott as a referee but question the decision-making process which has led to him being dispatched to Anfield once again.

The former chief executive of the PGMOL (now Pro Ref) posted on X: ‘A top-class referee, but not a very good appointing procedure by his bosses’.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

It’s a strong show of faith by Pro Ref chief executive Howard Webb to assign Barrott to what is always the most high-profile fixture in English football, and arguably world football.

Liverpool fans might be forgiven for not being able to summon much enthusiasm over the appointment, given the official’s previous at Anfield this season.

In August, it was he who awarded Nottingham Forest a penalty in their 2-2 draw against the Reds when Neco Williams went to ground under a challenge from Alisson Becker. The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents Panel subsequently adjudged that the spot kick was wrongly given.

While there are clear critera which must be observed when appointing match officials to specific fixtures – any officials from Merseyside or Manchester are obviously ineligible for Sunday’s clash at Anfield – seeing Barrott assigned to yet another Liverpool home game does seem anomalous.

Recent findings suggest that we just hope – for his sake as much as anyone else’s – that the main talking point after the final whistle isn’t a controversial and decisive error on his part. The last thing we need is yet more dubious refereeeing affecting the Reds.

Tech Report: How Kelly Rowland Keeps Her Eczema Flare-Ups Under Control During Winter

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1103 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, wintertime can bring everyone down with its colder weather and less sunlight.
  • That’s the case for Grammy-winning singer, actress, and Destiny’s Child alum Kelly Rowland, who has been living with eczema since her 20s.
  • “[You] don’t know what the environment is going to give you—because mine is also environmental—or what the weather is going to give you,” Rowland told Healthline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, wintertime can bring everyone down with its colder weather and less sunlight. But for those with eczema, this time of year can wreak havoc on their skin, too.

That’s the case for Grammy-winning singer, actress, and Destiny’s Child alum Kelly Rowland, who has been living with eczema since her 20s. During the winter months, she often dreads the cold.

“[You] don’t know what the environment is going to give you—because mine is also environmental—or what the weather is going to give you,” Rowland told Healthline.

Cold weather and indoor heating can reduce humidity, drying out the skin and triggering or worsening eczema flare-ups.

“[What we know] about the skin barrier is that it really is like a gate or wall against the outside world,” Camille Howard-Verovic, MD, a dermatologist at Active Dermatology, told Healthline.

According to recent reports, in healthy skin, the barrier controls what enters and leaves the skin. However, for people with eczema, Howard-Verovic said they have skin barrier dysfunction, which allows substances such as allergens and irritants to penetrate the skin.

Cold weather can increase transepidermal water loss, a process in which moisture escapes through the skin’s outer barrier and evaporates into the surrounding air.

According to recent reports, “People with eczema have a tremendous amount of transepidermal water loss, so you’re just drier,” mentioned Howard-Verovic. “[You’re] not holding onto the water as well, so that causes the itching and the rash that we feel when we have eczema.”.

Rowland first noticed eczema flares behind her ears as well as on her elbows, arms, and the back of her knees.

“[It] looked like a rash, so that’s what I thought it was all this time, and I dealt with it for so long until after I had my son and then it started to get worse on my face,” she stated.

She eventually went to a dermatologist who diagnosed her with moderate-to-severe eczema, a chronic inflammatory skin condition that can cause intense itching, painful skin cracking, thickened skin, and redness or swelling.

When Rowland learned that eczema can be genetic, it made sense to her.

“I remember seeing massive rashes on [my mom’s] neck and her arms…so she had it, and I guess I was the lucky one,” said Rowland.

At first, she tried eliminating foods that she thought might be triggers. She also bathed in oatmeal.

“[I] literally have had a tub full of oatmeal, like literally went to the store to get store-bought fresh oats,” she said. “I tried everything, and it doesn’t help until you go talk to a doctor about it.”.

At first, she tried prescription topical medications but found them cumbersome.

“I don’t have the time, if I’m being honest, and we live in a world that is moving so fast…I started buying like three tubes of whatever it was I was using and losing it; it was just too much for me,” Rowland mentioned.

According to recent reports, rowland said she found relief with Ebglyss, a prescription injectable medication for moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis. She has also partnered with Eli Lilly and Organization, its manufacturer, to raise awareness about eczema.

Rowland remarked she’s sharing her experience to help others living with eczema, including people she’s met who have experienced greater challenges managing the condition.

“One lady was telling me about how she’s having a tough time [looking] in the mirror cause she doesn’t know who’s looking back at her, and she saw her skin before eczema and after,” said Rowland.

When she first had symptoms, she mentioned she felt embarrassed, too.

“[Because] it was just in the middle of my arm space and…[if I] put out my hand to shake someone’s hand, you don’t know if somebody’s judgy,” she mentioned.

Rowland hopes being open about her condition will encourage others to advocate for themselves and talk with their doctor about treatment options.

Because eczema can look different on deeper skin tones, Howard-Verovic noted that a dermatologist can help make the correct diagnosis.

“Some people may not even know that they have eczema,” she said. “We know that eczema is a rash; it can appear red on certain skin tones, and it can be grey or white on certain skin tones, so it can look a little different.”.

In addition to medication, Rowland remarked managing stress helps reduce her eczema flare-ups.

It has been revealed that “Before [when] I went on tour, because I was under so much stress, it flared up like crazy, like you wouldn’t believe,” she said. “We were in the back trying to figure out how to cover certain things up, and we figured some of it out, and some of it was really tricky, but what helped was when I actually just calmed down…not that it helped overnight, but it did just kind of bring the flare down.”.

She stated red light therapy, feeling grounded outside without her shoes on, getting vitamin D from natural sunlight, and cooking are ways she reduces ongoing stress.

Sources indicate that “Cooking calms me when my kids aren’t here, and I have a really good [Zen] playlist on,” said Rowland. “[If] you ask me a question [in those moments], I might give you my heart; I’m just so happy.”.

She also tries to cut back on sugar, which she believes triggers flares.

Another way to reduce flares, according to Howard-Verovic, is to avoid hot showers, especially in the winter.

“[We] know eczematous skin likes lukewarm water,” she remarked.

Because Howard-Verovic and her daughter both live with eczema, she set a rule about when it’s time to get out of the shower.

According to recent reports, “[If] you see condensation on the bathroom mirror, you’ve spent too much time in the shower,” said Howard-Verovic. “[That] really hot, hot water feels really good in that moment…but when you get out all that water evaporates, and there’s no moisture in the atmosphere, and it dries your skin out, and now your skin is unhappy again.”.

If you prefer to take baths, she noted use gentle cleansers.

“[There] are bleach baths for really, really bad flare-ups,” she noted.

Diluted bleach baths are sometimes recommended for people with eczema, but they should only be used according to a healthcare professional’s instructions.

Recent findings suggest that as soon as you get out of the shower or bath, Howard-Verovic remarked to apply a quality moisturizer to your damp skin. According to the National Eczema Association (NEA), lotions containing the following ingredients can help ease dry skin associated with eczema.

To help identify appropriate products, look for ones that have the NEA’s Seal of Acceptance.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A week after Waymo was banned from operating on California freeways, the autonomous rideshare service has now paused freeway operations across the United States.

It has been revealed that the California-based startup unveiled the temporary pause on Wednesday, November 18, although it actually began on November 11. Normally, Waymo offers freeway service in the San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Miami, and Austin. The Associated Press cited a Waymo statement saying it is temporarily restricting “commercial freeway rides in all markets where we operate that service.” However, Waymo stated it would continue freeway testing with trained autonomous specialists at the wheel.

It has been revealed that it is not immediately clear when the freeway pause will be lifted. California initiated the ban last week after multiple incidents of Waymo vehicles driving into construction zones or disobeying orders from law enforcement; the state DMV stated an incident on November 5 and another on November 6 drove the regulatory agency to ban autonomous freeway operations.

“The Department determined that Waymo’s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present,” California DMV spokesperson Jonathan Groveman stated to the Associated Press. “The Department determined that Waymo’s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present.”.

Road & Track has reached out to Waymo for comment, and will update the story if we learn more.

#75238. BYD’s folding steering wheel isn’t a concept — it’s in a $49K SUV now

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1133 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

BYD’s folding steering wheel isn’t a concept — it’s in a $49K SUV now

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1133 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, BYD rolled out a production SUV today with a steering wheel that folds flat into the dashboard.
  • In a recent development, automakers and suppliers have been parading folding wheels on concept cars for about a decade.
  • Industry observers note that the whole thing hinges on steer-by-wire.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, BYD rolled out a production SUV today with a steering wheel that folds flat into the dashboard. It comes standard on the top trim of the Fang Cheng Bao Tai 9, which sells for 329,900 yuan (about $49,000) in China.

In a recent development, automakers and suppliers have been parading folding wheels on concept cars for about a decade. This is the first one customers can actually order, according to BYD.

Industry observers note that the whole thing hinges on steer-by-wire. There’s no steering column physically connecting the wheel to the front wheels, so the wheel is just an input device, and BYD can put it wherever it wants.

It has been revealed that on the Tai 9, it swings through 180 degrees on a hidden hinge and drops into a compartment in the dash in about 10 seconds. A panel closes over it, and a tray table folds out where the wheel used to be. Only the airbag remains outside of the compartment – keeping it useful with the steering wheel deployed or hidden.

It only folds when the vehicle is parked. Fang Cheng Bao pairs it with a driver’s seat that reclines to 165 degrees, so the pitch is simple: fold the wheel, lie back, and eat, nap, or play games while you charge or wait. The brand claims 80% of the driver’s area becomes usable space and rates the folding mechanism for 80,000 cycles.

When it’s deployed, it’s a regular D-shaped wheel with a full rim and physical buttons. No yoke. That’s a nice change from Tesla and Mercedes, which paired its latest steer-by-wire system on the EQS with a yoke.

At the launch event, Fang Cheng Bao general manager Xiong Tianbo mentioned the industry had been talking about folding steering wheels since 2016 without ever getting one into mass production. He added that BYD is using the same type of motor it develops for humanoid robots to move the wheel, a first in one of its cars.

Here’s Fang Cheng Bao’s official video of the feature:.

Industry observers note that china’s newly introduced national standard for steering systems took effect on July 1, 2026. It dropped the long-standing requirement for a mechanical link between the steering wheel and the road wheels, as long as the system meets redundancy and fail-safe rules.

According to recent reports, before that, steer-by-wire needed special approval. Nio’s ET9 was the first car in China to get it, back in December 2024. In the US, Tesla’s Cybertruck already uses it, and Mercedes is bringing it to the EQS this year.

Folding wheels themselves have stayed on show stands. BYD’s own Denza brand revealed one on the Z concept at Shanghai in 2025. Autoliv and Tensor called theirs the “world’s first foldable steering wheel” at CES in January, for a Tensor Robocar they expected to reach volume production in the second half of 2026. Hyundai Mobis has been showing one for years.

Recent findings suggest that tesla went the other way with the Cybercab: no wheel at all. But the prototypes testing on public roads have a Cybertruck steering wheel bolted onto an exposed column, because a human still has to be able to drive.

Sources indicate that the Tai 9 is Fang Cheng Bao’s biggest SUV yet. It’s 5,270 mm (207.5 in) long with a 3,130 mm wheelbase and six seats in a 2+2+2 layout. It’s also the first model on BYD’s newly introduced DMS hybrid platform.

A 1.5-liter turbo engine works with front and rear electric motors for a combined 400 kW (536 hp), and 0 to 100 km/h takes 4.8 seconds. The 66.48 kWh second-generation Blade battery supports BYD’s flash charging and delivers 310 km (193 miles) of electric range on the WLTC cycle. Rear-wheel steering, LiDAR, and BYD’s God’s Eye B driver assistance system are standard.

There are three trims: 279,900 yuan (about $41,700), 299,900 yuan, and 329,900 yuan. Only the top one gets the folding wheel.

Fang Cheng Bao sold 43,872 vehicles in October, up 41% year-over-year, mostly on the strength of the Tai 7. That model is now heading overseas: BYD sells it in the UK as the Ti 7. BYD hasn’t stated anything about exporting the Tai 9.

Sources indicate that it is not only that these technologies are impressive, but it is the speed at which they are being put into market by some of these Chinese car companies like BYD. They are moving further and further away from the competition but its understandable with the insane competition between car makers in China that they almost have to maintain and edge.

We’ve seen this at pretty much every auto show since the mid-2010s: a steering wheel slides away so the “driver” can relax while the car drives itself. It never shipped, for many reasons, but with steer-by-wire and autonomous driving now becoming reality, BYD is making the jump.

The Tai 9’s wheel only folds when you’re parked, so right now it’s a lounge feature. Recline the seat, stow the wheel, flip out the tray, and watch a movie while you charge. Is that a gimmick? A little. But Chinese EV buyers spend a lot of time in parked cars, and fridges, screens, and lie-flat seats sell cars there for a reason.

The bigger deal is underneath. The wheel can only fold because the Tai 9 is steer-by-wire, and BYD is putting that in a roughly $49,000 family SUV less than five months after China made it legal. After Cybertruck and now Mercedes with the EQS, we might be seeing the first steps of steer-by-wire actually becoming a more widely adopted technology.

Industry observers note that turn off reality TV and turn on the bald eagle cams. It’s all the drama you need.

Recent findings suggest that when internet-famous bald eagle Shadow seemingly welcomed a mysterious upcoming female into his nest earlier this week, many fans have questioned the whereabouts of Kaydee. After the death of Shadow’s longtime partner Jackie in August, he had been spotted spending time with the 4-year-old banded female eagle named KD1 (later renamed Kaydee). It seemed like the eagles might head into mating season as a pair, but after the arrival of a new, large female, it’s unclear how the relationships will all shake out.

Industry observers note that since the appearance of the mystery female, nicknamed Significant Beautiful Visitor or BBV by some fans, Kaydee has disappeared from view of Friends of Big Bear Valley (FOBBV)’s two cameras. She was last spotted by the cameras on November 14 in the Roost Tree, according to FOBBV. Despite concerns that she may be injured or had left the area, wildlife photographers have continued to document Kaydee’s presence near Big Bear Lake as recently as November 18.

In a recent development, photographer Alla Shumko shared photos of Kaydee perched near Big Bear Lake on November 18. Kaydee’s double bands are visible as she observed a scuffle between younger eagles fighting over fish.

Sources indicate that mating season is well underway, so viewers of FOBBV’s 24/7 livecams have been watching closely for signs that Shadow has selected a new partner. Shadow has worked with both Kaydee and the new eagle on nest maintenance and shared “beaky kisses” with each female, both signs of bonding in bald eagles. Bald eagle mating involves a bit of aerial acrobatics—copulating pairs can be seen in what’s called a “cartwheel display,” in which they lock talons in mid-air while tumbling down to the ground. Male eagles do not have an external phallus, so mating occurs via a touch of cloacas. Vocalizations can typically be heard during the act, which lasts about 7 to 12 seconds, according to Raptor Resource.

As this is nature, we humans can’t predict or influence who Shadow will pick as a upcoming partner. Or if he picks at all. All we can do is watch and wait and let nature take its course.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s been two years since Lego and Formula 1 first partnered up to translate the excitement of the grand prix grid into tiny, plastic, painful-to-step-on brick form. But while the race cars were a realistic low-polygon tribute to the life-size real things, the minifigures that accompanied them were fairly generic. Until now, that is, because the upcoming Lego Speed Champions lineup features all 11 teams on the 2026 grid and all 22 full-time drivers, rendered with realistic driving suits and customized hair.

Industry observers note that declared at the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix against a backdrop of several giant minifigures and a full complement of Lego-clad go-karts (now updated with neon LED light strips for the full Vegas experience), this next batch of Speed Champions sets will go on sale March 1, 2027. That makes for plenty of time to build all 11 before the first race of the season in Bahrain, although it’s also yet another thing to wait for during the off-season.

Arvid Lindblad, driver for the Visa Cash App Racing Bulls Team, made at appearance at Lego’s press announcement, and posed with both his large and small Lego likenesses. Asked about his thoughts on the result, the British driver said: “Awesome, nailed it. They got the hair perfect,” adding that, “I’ve always loved Legos, though I never imagined having my own minifigure.”.

And speaking of hair, yes, the Valteri Bottas minifigure is rocking a mullet. Each plastic hairpiece was approved by the respective drivers. “When we pitched the the hairstyles to the teams and the drivers, they absolutely loved it,” mentioned Will Thorogood, the Lego designer who led this effort. “They all thought it was as funny as we did.”.

Another key part of bringing out the driver’s personality is the helmets, which are “far more detailed than any helmet we've ever done before with the with the Lego production,” according to Thorogood. Lando Norris’s helmet, for example, “has all the blob details on it” as well as a minifigure Easter egg hidden in the design. Each driver also comes with two facial expressions on opposite sides of the minfigure head; Charles Leclerc’s visage is either relaxed in sunglasses or a more serious grimace, both with the Ferrari driver’s stubbled mustache and goatee.

The cars themselves reflect the fresh regulations and, indicates Thorogood, “as you look closely, you'll see every single one is built completely differently to capture all the aero details and principles that each of the teams has employed.” These too feature several Easter eggs for Lego fans, such as suspension wishbones made from wizard wands and rear diffuser strakes made from minifigure meat cleavers.

Measuring 7.5 inches long and 2.5 inches wide, the Speed Champions sets will be priced at $29.99 when they go on sale next year. More photos and details are viewable now on the Speed Champions section of the Lego Website.

Industry observers note that executive Editor Mike Austin has worked as a writer, editor, and occasional video host across titles such as Car and Driver, Autoblog, Popular Mechanics, and Hemmings (plus a few more). Prior to joining Road & Track he finally put his engineering degrees to use as an EV analyst. His personal cars skew slightly oddball, including a 1991 Honda Beat, 2001 Volkswagen Eurovan, 1987 Alfa Romeo Spider, and 2007 Saab 9-3 wagon.

Recent findings suggest that both electric SUVs use an 800-volt electrical architecture for ultra-fast charging. The IONIQ 5 can charge from 10% to 80% in about 20 minutes, while the IONIQ 9 takes around 24 minutes using a 350 kW DC fast charger.

Hyundai assembles the IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9 at the Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America outside of Savannah, Georgia.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Less than 400 adult North Atlantic right whales (Eubalaena glacialis) still exist in the wild, making them one of the world’s most critically endangered species.
  • In a recent development, “Naming right whales is a fun and creative activity for our research community, but it also allows an opportunity to connect with the whales on an individual level,” Amy Warren, an aquarium scientific program officer and name project coordinator, said in Anderson Cabot Center’s announcement.
  • The 2026 inductees also include Grand Slam (Catalog #3991) and Slide (Catalog #4991).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Less than 400 adult North Atlantic right whales (Eubalaena glacialis) still exist in the wild, making them one of the world’s most critically endangered species. Of those, 20 have officially received spiffy newly introduced names from conservationists at the New England Aquarium’s Anderson Cabot Center for Ocean Life. The researchers curate the annual North Atlantic Right Whale Catalog, and attach personable monikers to a select few baleen cetaceans in order to more easily monitor them. This year, it’s time to wave hello to Dodo, Volcano, and Dolly.

In a recent development, “Naming right whales is a fun and creative activity for our research community, but it also allows an opportunity to connect with the whales on an individual level,” Amy Warren, an aquarium scientific program officer and name project coordinator, said in Anderson Cabot Center’s announcement. “It can be hard to relate to Catalog #5299, but a whale named Nibbles is bound to be memorable.”.

The 2026 inductees also include Grand Slam (Catalog #3991) and Slide (Catalog #4991). The sister whales have a mother named Fenway (Catalog #2791), who was also named in honor of the Boston Red Sox. Grand Slam earned her fresh name thanks to her three patches of raised tissue known as callosities that resemble the bases on a baseball field. Meanwhile, Slide received their name due to the curved scar on her back that recalls someone sliding through home plate. Other right whale names this year include Goose, Donegal, and even Gonzo for the beloved Muppet.

“Although the names are intended to help researchers at sea, they also give the general public a better understanding of the individual whales,” added Caroline Mowdy, a spokesperson for Whale and Dolphin Conservation (WDC).

Collaborators at the WDC also created some lighthearted, yearbook-esque biographies for each whale. For example, Dolly (Catalog #4191), whose callosity looks strikingly similar to the late, great country singer’s larger-than-life hair, apparently loves the song, “Jolene.” Then again, who doesn’t?

“We see these whales and their families grow each year,” noted Mowdy. “Knowing them makes the tragedies even more tragic, but it also makes our determination to protect them even stronger.”.

On Monday, the North Atlantic Right Whale Consortium announced that there are roughly 382 North Atlantic right whales, representing a 1.8 percent drop in population size from the 2024 estimate. Their primary threats remain getting tangled in fishing line and vessel strikes.

In a recent development, however, even amid their struggles, the 2025–2026 right whale calving season saw the most calves born since 2009. A total of 24 calves were born, including a surprising late addition that was spotted in Canada in September.

#75232. Letter from the Editor-in-Chief: What a Missed Deadline Taught Me About Switching Off

Letter from the Editor-in-Chief: What a Missed Deadline Taught Me About Switching Off

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (835 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The piece you’re reading was supposed to be filed before I headed out on a long weekend to Italy for my wife’s birthday.
  • In a recent development, the main problem was I simply ran out of time to write the piece.
  • The other problem and consequence was that I carried a chunk of guilt into the break.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I missed a deadline last week. The piece you’re reading was supposed to be filed before I headed out on a long weekend to Italy for my wife’s birthday.

In a recent development, the main problem was I simply ran out of time to write the piece. An urgent stakeholder ask out of the blue, a couple of unanticipated work fire drills, and a long-standing evening social commitment earlier in the week made for a perfect storm, and something had to give.

The other problem and consequence was that I carried a chunk of guilt into the break.

In a recent development, it caught up with me at 6 am on the first morning, when I found myself drafting this column in my head. I should have been dozing peacefully. I continued to ruminate on my lengthy to-do list at work deep into day one as we headed from Venice into the Dolomites. My body was in Italy, but my brain was clearly still at my desk.

It has been revealed that switching off, particularly from work, is hard for most of us, and especially in an age of ubiquitous screens and wall-to-wall information competing for our attention. For me, that always-on reality plays a major role in the difficulties I have disconnecting from the daily grind.

I’m fortunate to love my job, and if I’m candid, I probably take a little too much of my identity from it. I hold on tight, and the phone in my pocket is an ever-present enabler.

According to recent reports, A meme that has stuck with me over the years goes something along the lines of being an adult is staring at medium screens all day only to come home and stare at a little screen while a big screen is on in the background. The irony is not lost on me that I came across this rather withering take on modern life while scrolling on stated little screen.

Regardless of the role the screen plays, psychologists who study employee well-being describe what I was missing for the early part of the weekend as “psychological detachment.” A state where you are genuinely able to not think about work while away from it. The science suggests it’s an crucial thing to work on.

A 2025 meta-analysis of 32 studies found that vacationing has a strong effect on well-being, and that the effect lasts longer than earlier research suggested. A second, smaller analysis of eight studies points to detaching from work, along with physical activity, as among the most helpful things to do while you’re off. In another study that tracked teachers during a two-week break, exhaustion, anxiety, and low mood all declined, while those who kept ruminating about work recovered less.

Industry observers note that whatever the science states, I know that for me the act of stepping away from work and being disciplined about not checking back in while I’m away is critical for my mental health and for staving off burnout. Getting out in nature and hiking or cycling or swimming keeps me present. It resets and recharges my batteries, and it tops up my creativity in a way that I find benefits what I am then able to bring back to the office.

Sure enough, as we drove deeper into the mountains on a crisp, blue-sky day, I could feel the golden autumnal hues and majestic rock formations drawing me in, closer to an elemental feeling of calm and happiness. That sense of equilibrium stayed with me all weekend, and while I’d be lying if I mentioned my mind didn’t occasionally drift to my desk, it was fleeting, with the knowledge that all the things would be waiting for me when I got back. Just like this piece was.

Industry observers note that with Thanksgiving on the horizon, and the holidays coming thick and fast thereafter, I’ll leave you with this bit of hard-earned advice: if your job is deeply entwined with your life and part of who you are, as mine is, time away can sometimes feel like a small act of disloyalty. It isn’t. In fact, it’s probably the most crucial thing you can do to remain faithful to your work ethic, and to yourself.

And if you’ll be working over the holidays, or you’re not working right now, or you don’t have the benefit of someone on hand to carry some of the load for you (shout out to all the Grannies out there), or your vacation looks very different from mine, that’s all okay. Find the pockets where and when you can: an evening, a walk, an hour in front of a screen, or better yet a book, and let work wait. Above all else, be kind to yourself. That’s how you really give yourself a break.

Robin Hough is the Editor-in-Chief of Healthline, and in addition to this regular Letter from the Editor column, he can be found every other Wednesday in our Healthline Wellness Wire newsletter.

Sources indicate that the most notable thing about Hyundai’s upcoming Elantra is its radical redesign, but there are enough updates under the skin to make this new compact sedan compelling for other reasons. The 2027 Elantra will arrive first with a mostly carryover engine, but the 2028 Elantra Hybrid comes with upgrades to its gas-electric powertrain that improve its power and mpg figures.

We already saw the Elantra’s upcoming sci-fi styling a few months ago when it was revealed globally, and the newly revealed U.S. version looks nearly the same. Angular lighting elements, sharply creased body lines, and futuristic details make this look far more distinctive than anything else in the mainstream compact segment. It’s also larger than before, with the wheelbase stretching by 1.2 inches, which provides extra legroom in the rear seat.

See all results for latest 2027 Hyundai Elantra for sale near 07011.

The standard model, arriving for the 2027 model year, has a carryover powertrain consisting of a 147-hp 2.0-liter inline-four and a continuously variable automatic transmission. The previous model offered a more powerful turbocharged engine in the N Line variant, but Hyundai has yet to announce any sort of performance version of the new Elantra—though we assume the full-bore Elantra N will eventually join the new generation.

The 2028 Elantra Hybrid has more power than before; its combination of a 1.6-liter inline-four and electric motors now makes 155 horsepower, an uptick of 16 horses compared with before. Hyundai estimates it will achieve up to 53 mpg combined, which is 1 mpg less than the outgoing model’s highest combined rating. It’s also notable that the hybrid model has a multilink rear suspension setup, compared with the nonhybrid’s twist-beam rear suspension.

Recent findings suggest that we like the look of the new interior, at least in the loaded Limited model we sat in, which incorporates nicer materials than you might expect in this segment. The dashboard layout is fresh and modern, with a standard 12.9-inch touchscreen protruding from the center of the dash. There’s also an optional slim digital gauge cluster that’s located near the base of the windshield. Hyundai’s latest Pleos Connect infotainment is in play here too, and it’s said to recognize more natural voice commands. Optional features include dual wireless charging pads and a Bang & Olufsen stereo.

Sources indicate that the ‘27 Elantra lineup starts with the base SE trim level and also includes SEL Sport and Limited trims. The hybrid lineup is similar, but the base model is called SE Blue. The outgoing Elantra is one of the most affordable cars on sale, and we hope the new one’s starting price won’t rise much above $25,000. The ‘28 Elantra hybrid, arriving later on, will cost a few thousand dollars more than that.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hailey Bieber is sharing her experience with premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD), a condition she claims has fueled her growing interest in women’s health research.

The Rhode Beauty founder recently announced a $5 million, three-year partnership with the Foundation for Women’s Health in an interview with Women’s Wear Daily (WWD).

“As a woman, I feel frustrated by the lack of research, the lack of awareness, the lack of certain conversation around it,” Bieber told WWD.

It has been revealed that motherhood has also shaped her perspective. Bieber welcomed her son, Jack Blues, with her husband, Justin Bieber, in 2024, describing the experience as a “really intense and special journey.”.

She also shared that she “struggled” with PMDD after giving birth, noting that there’s “not a lot of conversation or research around it.”.

“When we can identify with each other and have conversations relating to each other and talking about the things we’re dealing with and struggling with, I do think it makes it feel like less of a lonely journey,” Bieber said.

PMDD is a complexcondition that causes severe physical and psychological symptoms that typically occur in the days or weeks leading up to menstruation.

“What distinguishes PMDD from the more common PMS (premenstrual syndrome) is the severity of the symptoms and how significantly they can interfere with daily functioning,” Sari Eitches, MD, dual board certified physician and medical advisor to Terra Mare, told Healthline.

“Another defining feature is the timing: symptoms typically worsen in the week or two before a period, resolve within a few days after menstruation begins, and are minimal or absent during the rest of the cycle,” she stated.

Eitches also noted that PMDD is a chronic condition that can affect women at any stage of their reproductive lives, from adolescence through perimenopause, as long as they are having menstrual cycles.

“It is caused by a sensitivity to cyclic hormonal and neurotransmitter fluctuations, so [it] can occur in anyone with a menstrual cycle, though stages of hormonal fluctuation- including postpartum, weaning breastfeeding, and perimenopause- can be a trigger,” she added.

According to research published in 2024, approximately 1.6% of women and girls meet the strict diagnostic criteria for PMDD, equivalent to an estimated 31 million people worldwide.

A higher percentage of 3.2% have a provisional diagnosis, meaning a healthcare professional may believe a person has PMDD, but symptoms have not been measured for a sustained amount of time to meet the criteria for a confirmed diagnosis.

Eitches said that women with a personal or family history of depression or anxiety may be more prone to developing PMDD, as are women with a family history of PMDD itself.

It has been revealed that “PMDD is understood to be caused by a combination of heritable biological sensitivities and environmental triggers. These can include a history of trauma, chronic stress, and other chronic medical conditions,” she noted.

Eitches also stated that you should consider seeing a doctor if your symptoms are severe enough that they’re interfering with your ability to go to work or school, maintain your relationships, or participate in your life in the same way that you do during the other weeks of the month.

According to recent reports, to diagnose PMDD, a healthcare professional will review your medical history and symptoms and may perform a physical exam. They will typically ask you to track your symptoms over at least two menstrual cycles.

A PMDD diagnosis generally requires at least five symptoms, including at least one mood-related symptom, that occur before menstruation, improve shortly after a period begins, and significantly interfere with daily life.

The symptoms of PMDD may include:.

Treatment options for PMDD include prescription medications and over-the-counter treatments that may help relieve certain symptoms, such as:.

Eitches noted that cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) can also help manage symptoms.

Lifestyle changes may also help manage PMDD symptoms, including practicing relaxation techniques, eating a balanced diet, limiting sugary and salty foods, and getting regular physical activity.

Eitches noted that getting enough high quality sleep and resting on a consistent schedule is also important.

“I also recommend focusing on a whole-foods-based diet, limiting added sugar and caffeine, and avoiding cigarette smoking,” she noted.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kia’s EV lineup covers just about every size and price point, but it believes one thing is still missing: a truly cheap electric car. That’s about to change in 2027, when Kia aims to unveil a upcoming EV that could start at around $22,000 to $24,000.

It’s been 40 years since Kia introduced its first electric vehicle, the Besta EV, created so runners in the 1986 Asian Games wouldn’t have to breathe toxic fumes from the broadcast vehicle.

Kia has come a long way since the Besta EV hit the road, now offering a complete lineup of electric vehicles, from compact SUVs and hatchbacks to vans and three-row SUVs.

In Europe and the UK, Kia’s electric lineup consists of the EV2, EV3, EV4, EV5, EV6, EV9, and PV5 van, but the Korean automaker isn’t done yet.

“With no intention of resting on its laurels,” Kia noted, the brand looks to complete development of its first software-defined vehicle (SDV) by the end of 2027, an all-newly introduced B-segment EV hatchback.

It didn’t offer any other details on the upcoming EV, but Ted Lee, Kia’s executive vice president and head of global operations, told Auto Express that Kia and Hyundai are co-developing a latest dedicated EV architecture for an upcoming pair of entry-level electric cars.

Expected to arrive as the Hyundai IONIQ 1 and Kia EV1, the newly introduced EVs will compete with other entry-level electric cars like the Renault Twingo, which starts at about €20,000.

Industry observers note that lee said the EV1’s price will be highly competitive not just with other entry-level EVs, but also with small gas-powered cars, with prices expected to start in the €20,000 to €22,000 range, or about $22,000 to $24,000. And that’s without government incentives.

The EV2 starts at just €26,600 ($29,500) in Germany and other European markets as Kia’s current entry-level EV, so the price range would make sense.

While it will be Kia’s cheapest EV, Lee promised it would not cut corners in quality, design, or features.

It has been revealed that as its first SDV, the EV1 will feature Kia and Hyundai Motor’s latest-generation tech and software. Kia said the electric SDV will offer Level 2+ autonomous driving on highways. In 2029, Kia plans to expand to Level 2++, enabling it to operate in cities.

The upcoming EV will also use Hyundai’s SDV architecture (CODA), the Pleos Connect infotainment system, and Gleo AI, an in-vehicle Agenic AI.

According to recent reports, what will the EV1 look like? According to Auto Express, the entry-level EV will look a bit sportier and less boxy than the EV2 SUV. It could draw inspiration from the Vision Meta Turismo concept.

It also apparently won’t be based on the Picanto, Kia’s smallest gas-powered car. The Kia EV1 is expected to bring a unique style to the family.

This is good to see and makes sense, especially in Europe. I don't think Kia can go wrong making vehicles at so many different price points. It allows them to reach different segments and almost literally have something for almost everyone.

While all of Kia’s current EVs feature its ccNC infotainment system with dual 12.3″ instrument display and infotainment screens, plus a 5″ climate control panel, the EV1 could bring a simpler setup.

Industry observers note that like its other electric models, the EV1 is expected to receive the GT treatment. However, as an entry-level model, it may not use a dual-motor all-wheel-drive setup like the others.

Will Kia bring the EV1 to the US? Don’t get your hopes up. Kia has previously said the B-segment hatchback is designed for Europe. It could even be built alongside the EV2 at Kia’s plant in Slovakia.

It has been revealed that the good news? The EV3, Kia’s compact electric SUV, is now on sale in the US, starting at just $29,890.
